content.text: A Defensive pact is a multilateral agreement to defend against an extremely threatening neighbor. If the subject of the pact attacks one of the members, others will join the war like allies .
Membership in defensive pacts is influenced by threat , a value for each realm that increases during expansion and decays slowly over time.
Defensive pacts can be disabled in the game rules before the start of the game session.

Each county conquered adds between 2% and 15% threat. The exact amount depends mostly on your realm size(?). Claim and de jure wars generate less threat. Diplomatically vassalizing other rulers, or personally inheriting titles when you are already a ruler, also increases threat, but at a lower rate than war. A single source can add at most 50% threat.

If your vassals generate threat, some of this threat will be added to your own. This effect is much smaller than the effect of expanding on your own, since any given vassal is too small to generate much threat per county.

Threat decays at a rate between 0.21% and 0.4% per month. The exact amount depends on your military strength(?). With Monks and Mystics DLC, your Chancellor can be assigned to a job which increases threat decay.

Any land leaving your realm can reduce threat; this includes land lost via inheritance and conquest. However, land lost when a vassal becomes independent by obtaining a title with the same (or higher) rank as their liege will not reduce threat.

Granting independence to vassals decreases threat based on the number of counties freed. This encourages you to release outlying vassals, especially those who provide fewer levies due to de jure structure . Releasing your furthest vassals can also shrink defensive pacts, because fewer foreign realms will be close to your borders.

It is best if you already have a non-aggression pact with the vassal you plan to release, so they can't join defensive pacts; this is more important if the vassal being released is not of your religion. In addition, you can request an alliance.

At low levels of threat, defensive pact members are organized by religion group; note that rulers following a religion's heresies can join a pact alongside rulers following the mainstream religion. As threat increases, even infidels will fight together when defending against you.

rows: Minimum for defensive pacts against you
Religious groups other than yours will band together
Even your religious head and holy orders will join all wars

content.text: Threat caps at 100%. Thus, any threat beyond 100% will be lost.
Any realm can join a defensive pact against you if:

items.text: Your threat is at least 5%
The realm is not too large, primarily based on the number of holdings.
They are within 300 distance , or 400 distance if another religion group

content.text: AI will consider joining against you if:

items.text: You could attack me : Less than 80% troop strength and you have a CB (except "Make tributary" or "Humiliate nomad"?)
You're too big : Less than 20% your size in provinces
Pact needs assistance : pact is less than 70% strength, an existing member of their religion/culture/dynasty, and you are not

content.text: AI will then compute a score to decide whether to actually join:
They will join with a score above 110 and leave with a score below 70.
There are many things you can do other than simply waiting for threat to decay.

When fighting a war that would take you from 40% threat to 90% threat, declare as many other wars as you can handle at the same time. This is your last chance to attack moderately weak realms until (1) you can take on entire regions at once or (2) your threat decays.
With the Conclave DLC, if your council can vote on war declarations, be sure to have Glory Hounds voting if you wish to pursue this strategy and not cause tyranny and council discontent.

sections.heading: Attack targets who are not in defensive pacts

items.text: Attack new realms the day they are created, before they have a chance to join defensive pacts. It takes 1 day for them to join the pact. Make sure you have a CB ready.
Pick off vassals who are rebelling against their liege. They will never join the pact, when they are in a civil war.
If a realm has not yet joined a defensive pact, avoid gaining a CB on them until you're ready to attack. For example, only invite a claimant at the last minute.
Invade realms that are stronger than you on paper, increasing your de facto power through alliances or by hiring mercenaries and holy orders .

content.text: Pick off tiny defensive pact members by assaulting their holdings very quickly. If you completely occupy the target realm before the rest of the defensive pact shows up, you have 100% warscore and can declare the war over.

The main problem here is that levies cannot be raised when declaring war. Retinues , horde troops or mercenaries , on the other hand, can be mere days away from arriving in the province. These professional armies can be expensive, but there are many ways to gain wealth .
Another obstacle is the presence of upgraded castles; castles with fort level 6 and above cannot be assaulted; be sure to check the fort levels of castles before declaring war.

It is also helpful to know, when dealing with defensive pacts, that AI enemies will usually accept "enforce demands" if you have 80% warscore from occupation, even if other warscore factors are in their favor.
Which is also a way to sidestep the 99 % warscore cap before a major battle, since the latter can be hard to come by against big defensive pacts.

If a realm is slightly too large for a quick retinue assault, you can use a two step plan. First, find an excuse to be hostile to their armies and holdings. Use levies to weaken them as much as possible. Second, declare war on them and finish them off with retinues.
There are several ways to become hostile to a realm without incurring a truce or getting the defensive pact involved:

items.text: Being allied to their enemy:

children.text: Join an ally in a war where your target is on the other side
Join a coreligionist in a holy war
Join a rebelling vassal ( overthrow_ruler* rebellions only)

items.text: Being at war with their rebelling vassal
Raiding

content.text: Big defensive pacts often don't join a single war completely, that can be used in the following way:

items.text: first attack a small target that can be easily blitzed with complete occupation
repeat the first step, until the members of the defensive pact that aren't already at war with you are too small to be a threat
declare war against one of the remaining members of your choice (preferably a bigger realm that couldn't have been easily blitzed)
finish the war(s) against the small target(s), then the war against the last target can be fought without involvement of (most of) the defensive pact

content.text: If a ruler that is supporting a defender as part of a defensive pact dies, their realm stops participating in that war.
This can be used, e.g. via assassinations , to either directly weaken the enemy when fighting a defensive pact, or setting up a worthwhile target realm for a "Divide and Conquer" strategy.

To insure that the targeted ruler dies (with a high likelihood) at the opportune moment, it's best to wait for one of the events that show that a murder attempt is under way before starting the wars, and to target non-paranoid rulers.

While having high threat, nomads can consider attacking other nomads; as they cannot build forts, nomadic attackers only have to occupy all nomadic capitals in the target realm to get 100% warscore (assuming the target realm does not have other landed vassals).

sections.heading: Support vassals in their external wars

items.text: Establish strong vassals near your borders, even if you normally prefer to have weak vassals .
Raid neighbors and destroy their armies, so your vassals are more inclined to declare war.

children.text: Alternatively, raid your vassals' targets as they fight their wars.

items.text: Assist vassals with cash gifts, defeating their enemies' armies, or (depending on the CB) joining their war
It helps to have a large family .

Use favors to arrange marriages with infidels. You probably won't be able to buy a favor from a ruler who is in a defensive pact against you, but you might be able to buy a favor from their heir for use later.
You can even create a non-aggression pact with a betrothal, immediately break the betrothal, and attack. This is considered "gamey".

Making a realm your tributary forces them out of a defensive pact without increasing threat. It also increases your effective strength (since you can call tributaries to war) without allowing stronger realms to join the defensive pact.
Good against empires or any other realm from which you can't take a significant fraction of land in a single war.
If you do get a good CB against them later, you can release them from tributary status and immediately attack.
Forcing tributaries to join your wars may weaken your tributaries enough to trigger revolts. You can then declare wars on the revolts freely.
Use the CB for a tributary type which persists through succession.
When you conquer territory, any defensive treaty formed will be against your liege lord, who is perceived as the ultimate owner of this territory, and won't be triggered by future wars you initiate.
This means that vassal khans can expand with greater impunity than their Khagan.

sections.heading: Arrange to peacefully regain kingdoms granted independence

content.text: Find an unlanded father (who you expect to die within 10 years) without other landed family to avoid complications, and his eldest son (in good enough health to outlive his father).
Give the son a county and a viceroyalty kingdom.
Give the father the target kingdom.
Grant the father independence, lowering threat level.
When he dies, his son should inherit the kingdom but remain your vassal because he had a same tier title in your empire as the one he gained.
You do not gain threat when a vassal inherits land (unless the inherited realm accrued its own threat) so you've lost threat and a kingdom, but regained the kingdom without the threat.

Other PDS grand strategy games have related mechanics: [1]

items.text: Victoria 2 has Infamy . Internally, it is called BadBoy .

Europa Universalis IV has a more nuanced version of threat called Aggressive Expansion , a relation modifier that indicates how threatened each nation is by your actions. When Coalitions form in EU4, they can act aggressively to dismantle a threat.
